how: The opening call recruits flag converters, and a later proposal specifies a shared time and coordinates.
A participant judges the attempt outnumbered and recommends defending another flag instead.
A participant answers the initial request by reporting a tile placed.
A one-line answer explicitly joins the proposed heart takeover.
The proposal receives an explicit bare join, supporting the local call-and-answer relation without establishing that each reader owes an answer.
A later viewer asks what the achieved picture depicts, and the coded thread supplies no answer.
A capacity-based recommendation to stop does not establish stressful withdrawal or a repaired quarrel between members.
The opening caller proposes a flag project, satisfying the starter role independently of later participation.
Starting and calling can occupy one passage, so their functions need not appear as successive observed stages.
A national flag is proposed as the room's mark and another participant attempts an additional picture.
A tile-placement report makes individual building work visible in the thread.
A participant reports having made only the red part of another picture.
The request receives a direct report of placing a tile, supporting reported participation after the call.
A location question receives coordinates, and another turn identifies the same anchor point.
A coordinate answer can locate the work without settling design disagreement or supplying an agreed pixel template.
A participant's small screen makes locating the image difficult and occasions a request for its position.
A keeper reports watching for two hours because the picture is more interesting than studying.
Visible proposals and joins do not establish whether leadership or work-division decisions occurred outside these messages.
Individual tile reports do not establish whether scripts or spare accounts also contributed.
Public location-sharing does not establish a separate planning chat or prove that none existed.
Posting target coordinates establishes no hiding of plans or infiltration of rival venues.
A small screen is a device constraint without evidence of a site fault or a technical fix.
Participants replace changed tiles and explicitly aim to preserve the picture in its known form.
A changed-tile report receives explicit agreement that keeping the achieved picture unchanged is the task.
Maintaining an existing picture can coexist with another participant attempting an additional picture elsewhere.
The repair report identifies a changed tile without investigating its placer's affiliation or motive.
Repairs are evidenced without a demonstrated move from maintenance strain to scripts or spare accounts.
Prospective site choices change across small flags and hearts, while any prior loss remains unestablished.
Alternative target proposals do not establish rebuilding after the room's work was erased or overrun.
A capacity judgment precedes another proposed target, but the stated selection reasons do not establish insufficient hands as the cause of moving.
A participant recommends helping another flag without establishing that assistance was delivered or reciprocated.
A proposal to help another flag can arise during an initially outnumbered attempt before the documented upkeep phase.
The speaker explicitly gives being outnumbered as the reason to recommend defending another flag instead.
A speaker judges conversion acceptable because another copy remains, without an observed exchange between opposing positions.
A one-sided duplicate-copy justification can state a fairness rule before any recorded debate over covering others.
The duplicate-copy justification supports conversion rather than an act of sparing another work.
Takeover proposals do not establish a border agreement, truce, or the target's consent.
Proposed help for another flag does not establish coalition membership.
A second building location does not establish a host's rule or permission to build there.
Recommending help does not establish a member carrying proposals between rooms.
A suggestion to help another national flag does not establish dual membership or divided loyalties.
The proposals contain no authority disclaimer or request for a representative, leaving the revised process unobserved.
Without an evidenced agreement, the bounded agreement-to-refusal arrow cannot be tested.
Watching and repairing do not establish subsequent border negotiations.
The conversion justification does not establish restraint produced by a negotiated border.
The proposal to help another flag contains no preceding border bargain.
Repair reports do not establish upkeep leading to coalition membership.
A mock civic reward makes a joke from the achievement, and an appreciative reply plays along.
National references in a new celebratory joke do not establish inherited lore or an existing national in-joke carried into the canvas.
Targets are justified by colours, few changed pixels, and spare copies without evidence of a prior tie naming a rival.
Practical conversion proposals do not establish a quarrel carried in from before the canvas.
A public project call and joining answer do not establish formation of a new room around the mark.
The mock award and appreciative reply supply no dispute over offensive joking or language.
Canvas-related joking does not establish host-level April Fools framing.
The call and its answers establish no rules containing canvas talk.
A help request alone establishes neither a canvas-post flood nor moderation caused by it.
An unwanted tile does not identify a member attacking the mark because of objections to canvas posts.
A success title receives congratulations, and the later mock reward receives an appreciative reply.
Reported acquisition and celebration are present, but the edited acquisition statement does not establish their precise timing or causal link.
Announcing success can precede ongoing repair rather than imply that maintenance is finished.
Celebration can precede a later viewer's unresolved question about what the picture depicts.
The success announcement precedes the documented repair exchange without establishing that celebration caused maintenance.
The success announcement precedes the later identification question without establishing why that question arose.
The citable success title does not establish what its associated image records or its archival purpose.
Celebration and mock reward do not establish a decision to carry the effort beyond the canvas.
A question about the live picture before closure cannot test disputes over the versions retained after placement ends.
A congratulatory reply does not establish that the mark brought its author into the room.
A joking promise to contact an official does not establish real outreach or acknowledgement.
Celebration is evidenced without an established transition into archival recording.
The success title and identification question do not establish recording that motivates continued organisation.
Participants propose converting existing flags and hearts into the desired mark.
Calling for conversion can itself constitute the original building method rather than follow a separate recruitment stage.
Participants select conversion targets by existing colours and the small number of pixels requiring change.
Capacity-based refusal cannot establish principled restraint when the same speaker subsequently proposes another conversion.
The conversion proposals do not establish subsequent negotiation or an invoked truce.
The success title identifies no defeated rival and establishes no exchange of contest talk.
Conversion and celebration are evidenced without a transition into a contest conducted against a rival room in talk.
